items.title: Dashboard Trap — stop building dashboards to check data
items.summary: A veteran dev's 3-step agent workflow replaces metric dashboards: the agent does the looking and reports only what needs action.
items.opsAngle: The digest→review→task flow follows this pattern. Apply the same to /ops metrics: agents surface exceptions instead of new dashboard panels.

items.title: Blast Radius — grep hook that traces call chains before edits
items.summary: One dev's agent got sharper after a hook that traces any function's call chain + blast radius before editing. Token usage dropped 50%.
items.opsAngle: Would slot into the existing guardrail/hook system as a pre-edit Claude Code hook.

items.title: Animation Vocabulary — a skill that teaches AI motion terms
items.summary: A Linear design engineer built a skill teaching the exact terms pros use, so AI builds the animation you pictured (2.4K bookmarks).
items.opsAngle: Relevant to HDS motion work (check-motion / reduced-motion gates already exist; vocabulary could improve motion specs).

items.title: Loop Engineering — Andrew Ng's 3-loop framework
items.summary: Ng's take on loop engineering and why devs are turning into product managers (5.4K likes).
items.opsAngle: The vendored site agent literally runs this pattern (refineLoop: produce → evaluate → retry-with-feedback). Useful for tuning iteration budgets.

items.title: Claude Sonnet 5 released — agentic, cheaper than Opus
items.summary: Anthropic shipped Sonnet 5: plans, browses, runs terminals on its own; closing the gap with Opus 4.8 on reasoning/tool use/coding at lower cost.
items.opsAngle: Candidate for the agent's model tiering (lib/agent/llm.mjs MODELS) — could take generation duty from Opus if quality holds; check pricing first.

items.title: gh-address-comments — clear a pile of PR review comments in one pass
items.summary: OpenAI skill that analyzes unresolved PR threads, applies fixes, and resolves comments; checks in before disagreeing.
items.opsAngle: Concept already covered by Claude Code PR babysitting here, but the batch-resolve UX is worth stealing for review workflows.

items.title: Top 30 prompt techniques that actually work (2026)
items.summary: Newer models interpret instructions literally — structured techniques (XML tags, explicit success criteria) beat legacy prompt tricks.
items.opsAngle: Quick pass over lib/agent prompts (enrich/generate/judge SYSTEM strings) against this list.
